subject: Parallelization in Stan for single chain?

messages.author: f33789bdc05b5462
messages.subject: Parallelization in Stan for single chain?
parts:
Dear Stan users list,

I am currently trying to run stan on eye-movement models, which require some calculations on a grids and the computation time and memory demands are quite high (seconds per sample + 20-40 Gig memory). Thus it would be very interesting to parallelize some of the code, at least over data from different subjects which are independent calculations and can be parallelized trivially for each likelihood/gradient evaluation. On the other hand parallel chains are very limited by the memory constrains here and help very little, compared to the 50-100 cores I could have for these calculations easily.

So is there any way to code in stan to run in parallel? Or will there be in near future?

And in case this is not possible: Are there rules to keep the memory requirements of stan / it's autodiff algorithm low? (simply to run more parallel chains)

all the best
Heiko

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Parallelization in Stan for single chain?
parts:
> On Jun 15, 2015, at 6:57 AM, 'Heiko Schütt' via Stan users mailing list <stan-...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
>
> Dear Stan users list,
>
> I am currently trying to run stan on eye-movement models, which require some calculations on a grids and the computation time and memory demands are quite high (seconds per sample + 20-40 Gig memory). Thus it would be very interesting to parallelize some of the code, at least over data from different subjects which are independent calculations and can be parallelized trivially for each likelihood/gradient evaluation. On the other hand parallel chains are very limited by the memory constrains here and help very little, compared to the 50-100 cores I could have for these calculations easily.
>
> So is there any way to code in stan to run in parallel?
> Or will there be in near future?

We haven't even tried to get the multicore
matrix operations working, but it's on our to-do list.
At that point, some matrix ops will be much faster.

Our math library's getting more factored to the point
where it'd be possible to drop in replacements that
ran on GPUs, but that's a ways off because none of us
know how to do it.
> And in case this is not possible: Are there rules to keep the memory requirements of stan / it's autodiff algorithm low? (simply to run more parallel chains)

Vectorize whatever you can, use as many of the compound operations as
you can, and precompute results and reuse them rather than recomputing.
That is, don't doo foo(exp(x)) + bar(exp(x)) --- store that exp(x) and
use it twice.

In terms of writing out results, you can move parameters from transformed
params to locals in the model block.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Parallelization in Stan for single chain?
parts:
Another option is to do a parallelized EP-like algorithm where you break the data into 100 parts and fit Stan separately to each, using the EP-estimated cavity distributions as priors:
http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/unpublished/ep.pdf
A
